title: Injuria sine damno and damnum sine injuria

content.overview: Injuria sine damno (violation of a legal right without proven actual loss) is actionable. Damnum sine injuria (actual loss without violation of a legal right) is not. These maxims frame whether the claimant has a cause of action at all.

sections.heading: Injuria sine damno
sections.body: Where a legal right is invaded, the law presumes damage. Classic illustrations: Ashby v. White (wrongful denial of vote); Bhim Singh v. State of J&K (illegal detention — compensation for rights violation). The point is rights-protection, not a balance-sheet of financial loss.

sections.heading: Damnum sine injuria
sections.body: Competition or lawful exercise of rights may cause loss without creating a tort. Gloucester Grammar School and Mogul Steamship illustrate loss from lawful rivalry. The claimant must show an invaded legal right, not only economic harm.

sections.heading: Application method
sections.body: Identify the precise legal right claimed. If none, dismiss on damnum sine injuria. If a right exists, liability may follow even without special damage unless the tort requires proof of damage.

hypotheticals.question: A shopkeeper lawfully undercuts prices; a rival loses customers. Actionable?
hypotheticals.analysis: Absent unlawful means, conspiracy of a prohibited kind, or infringement of a legal right, this is damnum sine injuria. Lawful competition is not a tort.

enhancement.definition: Injuria sine damno means violation of a legal right without proof of actual pecuniary loss; damnum sine injuria means actual loss without infringement of a legal right.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Actionability depends on infringement of a legal right, not merely on economic loss.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Indian tort law is largely uncodified. The governing rules are developed through common-law principles, Indian judicial decisions and applicable legislation for particular fields; no statute should be treated as a general codification of this topic.

distinctions.title: Injuria sine damno
distinctions.left: Injuria sine damno: legal right violated; actual loss need not be proved.
distinctions.right: See the distinction described in the rule.

distinctions.title: Damnum sine injuria
distinctions.left: Damnum sine injuria: actual loss suffered; no legal right infringed, so tort damages ordinarily do not follow.
distinctions.right: See the distinction described in the rule.
